title: Quarterly roadmap: Dedicated capacity flexibility and autoscale OKR alignment
creator: Priya Nair
description: This ticket captures the Q1 roadmap and OKR alignment for making Dedicated capacity more flexible and cost-effective via autoscaling, predictive hedging, and time-windowed burst reservations. Outcome: a clear set of deliverables and gated experiments that move Dedicated from fixed reservations toward a hybrid commit+dynamic model while preserving SLOs for high-tier customers.
objectives_and_key_results: O1 - Improve Dedicated cost-efficiency: KR1 reduce avg cost-per-1M tokens across batch workloads by 22% by EoQ; KR2 increase average GPU utilization for reserved pools from 62% to 78%
O2 - Preserve latency SLOs during autoscale: KR1 maintain API p95 latency <= 250ms for 95% of traffic; KR2 reduce tail latency incidents by 50% compared to baseline
O3 - Operationalize hybrid commitments: KR1 launch predictive hedging MVP for burst capacity with documented SLAs and pricing; KR2 ship admin console controls for time-windowed bursting and caps
milestones: M1 - Jan (Research): telemetry spike analysis, prefix-level load shapes, and cost/latency trade matrix
M2 - Feb (MVP): predictive autoscaler prototype + 2 small-customer alpha (internal + 1 external), initial pricing proposal
M3 - Mar (Launch prep): console controls, billing integration, runbook, and canary rollout to Dedicated customers
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler can increase allocated GPU pool to cover 3x baseline burst for selected customers without violating latency SLO
Dashboards show per-customer fill rate and cost delta compared to static reservations
Pricing model and customer-facing docs published and approved by GTM
Runbook and rollback plan validated in chaos test with <15 minute mean recovery
success_metrics: Cost per 1M tokens down 22% for target workloads
No more than 2 production-severity latency regressions in Q1 from autoscale changes
Alpha customer retention and positive feedback (>=8/10) on flexibility
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscale increases contention and tail latency - Mitigation: conservative initial burst limits, KV cache pre-warming, and explicit routing by customer tier
Risk: Billing complexity for hybrid model - Mitigation: prototype clear line-item billing in sandbox and coordinate finance before GA
Risk: Sales/customer confusion - Mitigation: playbook + training + migration assistance for top 20 accounts
decision_log: 2025-01-28: Decided to prioritize predictive hedging MVP over full elastic autoscaler this quarter to limit blast radius
2025-02-03: Agreed to use per-prefix traffic heuristics for burst eligibility (ENG-2433) rather than per-API-key heuristic for faster iteration
2025-02-10: Pricing model chosen: tiered burst credits + usage surcharge; finance to validate net margin before GA
notes: 2025-01-24 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to 2 burst scenarios (short spikes <15m, scheduled time-windows)
2025-01-31 - Eng: data collection job landed (ENG-2201) to gather per-prefix latency-at-load curves
2025-02-07 - PM review: tightened success metrics to include fill-rate and cost delta per-customer
2025-02-12 - Design feedback: console controls should expose cap, priority, and alert thresholds (DES-612)
Follow-ups: schedule finance review (due 2025-02-20) and legal review for new pricing language
open_tasks: ENG: implement autoscaler safety gate (ENG-2568) - in progress
PM: finalize pricing wording with finance - owner Ethan Chen - due 2025-02-20
Design: console control mocks - DES-612 - waiting on review
retro_and_next_steps: Plan a 2-week alpha and collect SLO telemetry to validate hedging thresholds
If alpha meets success metrics, run a 4-week canary with 5 beta customers in April
Otherwise, iterate on conservative caps and caching strategies and re-evaluate
